messages.content: I’m done enough with the Northwest loop and need to start the Texas one. It’s Oct. 14-17: Monday late-morning counselor meeting near Fort Worth, Monday evening Dallas fair, Tuesday visits in Waco and Temple, and a Wednesday evening alumni event that may be somewhere between Austin and San Antonio. I’m trying to decide open-jaw into DFW and home from AUS or SAT versus a simple round trip. Hotels and rental car are not settled.

This is a north-to-south route, so the simple round trip may make the driving harder. Before I tighten the flight and hotel map, what time is the Fort Worth meeting, the Dallas fair, the Tuesday visits, and do you need to be home Thursday?

Fort Worth is 11:30 near TCU, Dallas fair is 6:30-8:30 at Market Hall. Tuesday: Waco high school at 9:00, Baylor counselor lunch at 11:30, Temple school at 2:15. Wednesday event is likely 6-8 but venue not final. I’d like to be home Thursday, no Friday stay.

Initial read: open-jaw wins unless reimbursement punishes the one-way rental. DFW in / AUS out is the cleanest if Wednesday is Austin or north Austin. DFW in / SAT out is best only if the event lands in San Antonio or New Braunfels. DFW round trip is simple on paper but adds 3+ hours of backtracking Thursday, or a bad late drive Wednesday after the event. AUS round trip is the worst fit because you would have to drive to Fort Worth before the 11:30 meeting. I’d plan DFW in and hold the return airport until the Wednesday venue firms up.
Could I fly in Monday morning, or am I kidding myself and should come Sunday night?

Same-day can work, but only with a nonstop that lands DFW around 9:15 or earlier. You need time to deplane, get the rental car, exit DFW, and drive 35-55 minutes to TCU. A 9:45 arrival is possible on paper but gives you almost no cushion for a late inbound, rental counter line, or Fort Worth traffic. If the clean flight lands after about 9:30, I would move to Sunday night.
Early Monday is fine for this trip. Include Delta if it’s clean, but I’m not taking a weird connection just for the carrier.

Then I’d use a practical flight rule: take the earliest nonstop into DFW that arrives before the buffer cutoff. If Delta has that, great; if Delta connects or lands closer to 10:00, use American or another nonstop into DFW. For the return, Austin usually gives you more workable SLC routings than San Antonio. San Antonio is only worth it if the event is truly south.
Assume no Sunday. How ugly is the road piece if Wednesday ends up Austin versus San Antonio?

If Wednesday is Austin or a north suburb, the route is clean: Dallas after the fair, early Tuesday drive to Waco, Temple after lunch, then continue to Round Rock or North Austin for Tuesday and Wednesday nights. If Wednesday is San Antonio, North Austin becomes a long evening return or a late hotel change; San Marcos, New Braunfels, or north San Antonio would be less painful. The pinch points are Monday DFW-to-Fort Worth after landing, Fort Worth-to-Dallas before the fair, and Tuesday Dallas-to-Waco. For that last one, I’d leave around 6:30 for a 9:00 visit.
I don’t love switching hotels every night. Could I do Dallas Monday and then one southern base Tuesday and Wednesday?

Yes, if the Wednesday venue is Austin, Round Rock, Cedar Park, or even San Marcos. After the Temple visit, you would keep moving south, check into the same hotel Tuesday and Wednesday, and avoid unpacking twice. If the event lands in downtown San Antonio, though, a North Austin base turns into a 90-120 minute drive each way depending on traffic. Then I’d switch the base to San Antonio or use San Marcos/New Braunfels as the compromise.
For hotels, I need to stay inside the university reimbursement range, breakfast included if I can get it, and decent food nearby after the evening events. Nothing fancy.

For Monday, I would not sleep in Fort Worth after the Dallas fair. Look at Dallas Market Center/Medical District, Las Colinas, or North Dallas near the fair, with the deciding factor being late dinner access and a clean route to I-35 for Waco. For Tuesday/Wednesday, if Austin is likely, look at Round Rock, Cedar Park, or the Domain/Arboretum area. Those areas have practical chain hotels, easier dinner options, and breakfast-included rates to verify. If San Antonio becomes likely, shift to New Braunfels or north San Antonio rather than central San Antonio.
My director asked whether staying in Waco Tuesday would make Wednesday easier because Waco hotels may be cheaper. Does that make sense?

Only as a cost play. Waco Tuesday saves some hotel money, but your last Tuesday stop is already in Temple, south of Waco. If you go back to Waco, you push the longer drive into Wednesday: about 1.5-2 hours to North Austin and closer to 3 hours to San Antonio before traffic or setup time. If the venue is likely Austin-area, continuing to Round Rock or Cedar Park after Temple is less stressful.
I can set one Wednesday counselor coffee wherever it helps. The alumni host just has not picked the restaurant yet.

Then place the Wednesday coffee near the eventual hotel base. If you choose Round Rock or Cedar Park, schedule the coffee there or at the Domain and keep Wednesday compact. If the event shifts south, make the coffee in San Marcos or north San Antonio. I would avoid putting the coffee in Waco because it anchors you north and lengthens the event-day drive.
Can you leave me with a plain comparison I can send for approval, including the drive-time risk?

Approval comparison: choose open-jaw unless the one-way rental fee is extreme. Working plan is SLC-DFW early Monday, arriving by about 9:15; pick up a one-way rental; Fort Worth meeting; Dallas Market Hall fair; Monday hotel in Market Center or Las Colinas. Tuesday drive early to Waco, then Temple, then continue south. If the alumni venue is Austin-area, stay Tuesday/Wednesday in Round Rock, Cedar Park, or North Austin and fly home Thursday from AUS. Use SAT only if the venue is south of San Marcos. Main risks: DFW arrival later than 9:30 jeopardizes the Fort Worth buffer; DFW round trip adds a tiring Thursday backtrack; Waco Tuesday is cheaper but moves the long drive to Wednesday.

messages.content: Update on Texas: Wednesday event is confirmed in Cedar Park, 6:00 to 8:00. I need to lock hotel areas. We get reimbursed up to about $185 before taxes. I’m thinking one Dallas-area night Monday and two nights north Austin, but my director still asked if Waco Tuesday is smarter.

Cedar Park simplifies it. I’d use one Dallas-area hotel Monday and one North Austin/Round Rock/Cedar Park hotel for Tuesday and Wednesday. Waco Tuesday only helps the nightly rate; it does not help the flow once your last Tuesday appointment is in Temple.

Monday fair is at Dallas Market Hall until 8:30. The Fort Worth meeting is near TCU. Tuesday is Waco 9:00, Baylor lunch 11:30, Temple 2:15. I’ll need food after the fair and again after the Cedar Park event.

Overnight sequence comparison: A) Dallas Market Center or Las Colinas Monday, then Round Rock/Cedar Park Tuesday-Wednesday: least stressful overall; Tuesday after Temple is about 50-75 minutes to the hotel, Wednesday is local, Thursday AUS is manageable. B) Waco Tuesday, Cedar Park Wednesday: cheaper possibility but adds a hotel change and a longer Wednesday drive. C) Stay south of Dallas Monday to shorten Tuesday: helps the Waco departure a little but usually sacrifices better late dinner choices after the fair. I’d choose A.
For the Dallas night, would you pick Market Center, Las Colinas, or something south toward Waco?

Market Center is best if you want to be off the road quickly after the fair. Las Colinas is a little farther after the fair but often has better chain-hotel value and plenty of restaurants. South toward Waco only makes sense if you are comfortable driving 20-35 minutes after the fair at night and you find a clear breakfast-included rate. My practical pick is Las Colinas if the rate is within cap; otherwise Market Center.
Can you name the hotel styles I should search? I don’t need a luxury place, just predictable.

For Dallas, search Holiday Inn Express, Hampton Inn, Fairfield Inn, or Home2 Suites in Market Center/Medical District and Las Colinas; verify breakfast is included on the rate because some nearby Hilton and Marriott brands charge separately. For the Austin side, search Round Rock/La Frontera, Cedar Park, or the Domain/Arboretum for Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Home2 Suites, SpringHill Suites, or Fairfield. Round Rock/La Frontera is likely the best price and food balance.
The Domain sounds easy for dinner but maybe over the cap. Would Round Rock make Cedar Park annoying?

No. Round Rock/La Frontera to Cedar Park is typically 20-35 minutes, and after the Temple visit it is an easy continuation south. It also keeps Thursday’s drive to AUS reasonable, usually 35-50 minutes if you leave with cushion. The Domain is nicer for restaurants, but it can cost more and may add traffic. Cedar Park is closest to the event but can be less convenient for the airport.
Okay, please answer the Waco question directly and give me the least-stressful overnight sequence.

Direct answer: do not stay in Waco Tuesday unless the savings are large enough to justify an extra hotel change and a longer Wednesday drive. Least-stressful sequence: Monday night in Las Colinas or Dallas Market Center after the fair, preferably a breakfast-included chain with late dinner nearby; Tuesday morning leave early for Waco; after Temple, drive to Round Rock/La Frontera or Cedar Park and stay there Tuesday and Wednesday; set the Wednesday coffee near that hotel; after the Cedar Park event, return to the same hotel; Thursday fly home from AUS. Round Rock/La Frontera is my first choice if it prices under the $185 cap, with Cedar Park second and the Domain only if the rate is surprisingly good.

messages.content: Last Texas piece: I’m ready to book flights. Delta can do SLC-DFW Monday arriving 9:35, but the return from Austin has a late Atlanta connection and gets me home after 10:30. American has SLC-DFW arriving 9:10 and AUS-DFW-SLC Thursday, home about 4:30, for a little less. Which would you choose?

I’d book American for this trip. The 9:10 DFW arrival gives a better cushion before the 11:30 Fort Worth meeting, and the Austin return gets you home at a sane hour without a long late connection. The Delta return adds fatigue without solving a schedule problem.
The Austin return connection in DFW is 65 minutes. Is that comfortable enough or should I worry?

Sixty-five minutes at DFW on one airline is workable for a domestic connection, but it is not roomy. If there is an 80- to 100-minute connection that still gets you home before dinner, I would pay a modest difference. If the choice is 65 minutes versus the late Atlanta return, I’d still take the 65-minute DFW option.
There is an American return leaving AUS 11:25, DFW 12:35, then DFW to SLC at 2:05, landing 3:55. It’s $32 more.

That is the better itinerary. The 90-minute DFW connection is much more comfortable, and landing in SLC before 4:00 is a strong return. I would book that over both the 65-minute version and the late Delta connection.
Good. Main cabin/economy, and I’ll pick a window if there’s one. Anything else to note for reimbursement?

Book main cabin rather than basic economy if seat selection or changes matter. Save the fare comparison and note the reason: DFW arrival improves the Fort Worth buffer, AUS return avoids the late Delta connection, and the open-jaw matches the approved DFW-to-Cedar Park route with a one-way rental.
Can you give me the final booking language?

Book American open-jaw: SLC to DFW Monday Oct. 14, arriving about 9:10 a.m. for the 11:30 Fort Worth meeting; AUS to SLC Thursday Oct. 17 via DFW, departing AUS 11:25 a.m., about a 90-minute DFW connection, arriving SLC about 3:55 p.m. Main cabin/economy; select a window seat if available. Reimbursement note: schedule reliability and shorter return justify choosing this over the late Delta connection; rental is one-way DFW pickup, AUS return.
